metadata.purpose: Fast-lookup orchestrator index with success probability weighting for intelligent exploit prioritization
metadata.success_weight_strategy: Higher success_weight = higher probability of exploitation success observed in real incidents. Enables orchestrator to mimic veteran pentester behavior by executing highest-probability exploits during early, low-detection-risk windows.
metadata.confidence_rating: Derived from categorical success_rate in playbook_registry.yaml (High→0.85, Medium→0.65, Low-Medium→0.55, Low→0.35)

phase_1_reconnaissance.strategy: Execute highest-success-weight reconnaissance playbooks. These are passive/low-risk and enable targeting for subsequent active phases.

phase_2_initial_exploitation.strategy: Execute highest-success-weight exploits (0.72-0.85) during low-risk window. These have proven success rates and quick execution times. Establish initial foothold.

phase_3_post_exploitation.strategy: Execute medium-success-weight exploits (0.65-0.80). Detection risk escalating. Chains enabled after initial foothold. Escalate privileges, exfiltrate data.

phase_4_advanced_persistence.strategy: Execute lower-success-weight exploits (0.50-0.62) only if detection risk permits. These are complex, time-intensive. Focus on persistence and evasion.

phase_5_fallback_strategies.strategy: Execute extreme-complexity exploits (success_weight <0.50) only as last resort. These have low success rates, very high complexity, maximum detection risk. Used when all standard exploits fail.

pseudocode: continue  # skip, detection risk too high
abort()  # detection too likely, exfiltrate and escape
strategic_routing_algorithm.explanation: This algorithm mimics veteran pentester behavior: (1) prioritize high-success-weight exploits first, (2) allocate early exploitation window to fast, high-confidence exploits, (3) reserve complex, low-success exploits for later phases when detection risk is already high, (4) abort when detection risk exceeds threshold, (5) escalate to human review when autonomous exploitation fails.
